result.title: Self-Improvement Memory Enables Continual Recursive Self-Improvement
result.summary: Harness optimization is often studied with a fixed policy model and benchmark. When either changes, the optimizer must decide which parts of an evolved harness to reuse or revise, but the harness alone may not explain why earlier edits were made or how they performed. In this work, we study Continual Recursive Self-Improvement (CRSI), a setting for continuing existing harness-optimization methods across compatible benchmarks or policy models. We propose Self-Improvement Memory (SIM) for the harness optimizer, rather than the task-solving policy. SIM groups edits by recurring harness problem and records their rationale, predicted and observed outcomes, and evaluation context. New attempts extend this history as optimization continues. In our experiments across four domains, SIM achieves higher final scores than harness-only and root-cause-only continuation in cross-dataset and pairwise cross-model comparisons. Across ten independent source runs in coding, paired continuations with SIM improve final scores by an average of 2.36 points over harness-only continuation ($p=0.003$).

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Continual Recursive Self-Improvement 设定，研究在更换基准或策略模型后继续既有 harness 优化流程，并给出 Self-Improvement Memory：按反复出现的 harness 问题分组记录编辑理由、预测与实际结果及评测上下文，供后续优化复用。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按问题分组记录改动理由、预测与实测结果」的记忆组织方式，可能为 LVR 中推理状态更新的贡献分配、轨迹训练数据的复用与跨任务延续提供核查线索，但对象是外层 harness 优化器而非模型内部 latent 视觉推理状态。
